title: Codfish with Starchy Vegetables, Puerto Rican Style

content.title: About
content.content: Codfish with starchy vegetables, Puerto Rican style is a traditional island dish where tender white cod is cooked together with root vegetables (sweet potato, yam, or other starchy tubers) and aromatic spices. The dish balances the light marine flavor of the fish with the natural sweetness of the vegetables, seasoned with garlic, oregano, adobo, and lime.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cod is one of the most popular fish in the Caribbean Sea thanks to its mild taste and low fat content.
Starchy vegetables like sweet potato are a staple in Puerto Rican cuisine, providing carbs and vitamins A and C.
The dish is often served with rice, beans, and a green salad to create a complete meal.
Traditional preparation involves slow braising in earthenware pots, which locks in the spice aromas.
Puerto Rico celebrates a "Fish Day" when this dish is prepared in large quantities for family gatherings.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Cod provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many seafood options, cod is very low in saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The fish is abundant in vitamin B12 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Starchy vegetables add fiber
items.content: Sweet potatoes and yams contribute dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Sweet potato is high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A for eye health and immunity.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including cod.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: While cod generally has low mercury levels, pregnant women and young children should limit intake.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Starchy vegetables can raise blood sugar; people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, typically as a portion of fish smothered in a spice‑rich sauce with a side of braised sweet potatoes or yams. Finish with a squeeze of fresh lime, chopped cilantro, and a drizzle of olive oil for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh cod refrigerated and use within 2 days. Store cooked leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze individual portions for up to 2 months.
